schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins

Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]

If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# FirstRun concept video, design

## Style Prompt
Apple keynote style on a light canvas. One idea per scene, large tight type, white cards with soft shadows, lots of empty space. Motion is calm and exact: short blur-fades between scenes, entrances timed to the spoken word, a slow push on every scene. Green means a step passed, red means it broke, blue is the single accent.

## Colors
- Background `#F5F5F7`
- Card `#FFFFFF`
- Ink `#1D1D1F`
- Muted `#6E6E73`
- Line `#D8D8DE`
- Pass `#1F8A3B`
- Fail `#D70015`
- Accent `#0066CC`

## Typography
- Geist 700 for headlines (SF Pro stand-in), Geist 400/500 for body.
- Geist Mono for commands, step labels and the FirstRun wordmark.

## What NOT to Do
- No dark cards, no gradients on text, no neon.
- Never redraw or recolor the neatlogs, Entire or cfo.ai logos. Use the files in `assets/logos/`.
- No made-up metrics. The example project is the fictional `acme`.
- No jump cuts. Every scene enters with a blur-fade.

# FirstRun Demo Video Production

The video is worth 20%, and the judges watch it before deciding how deep to read. The rule: 3:00 or less, and for each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai it shows architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result. This script covers all 15 points. The labels in brackets mark them.

The voiceover runs about 420 words, which fits 3:00 at a calm 140 words a minute. Every `<value>` is a real number you fill in on Monday. Never record a made-up number.

## The Voiceover Is Written Word for Word

**Beat 1, 0:00 to 0:15, the hook.** On screen: a red failed step in the terminal, then the title card.

> Your quickstart broke last week. You did not know. The first person who found out was a new developer, and they left. I built FirstRun, an agent that runs your quickstart before your users do.

**Beat 2, 0:15 to 0:45, the agent.** On screen: the architecture diagram, then a sped-up real run.

> Give FirstRun a docs URL. It reads the page and plans a runbook, one step per command. It runs every step in a clean container, like a brand-new developer. When a step breaks, it works out why, finds the fix, and retries. If it cannot tell a docs bug from intended behavior, it asks me once and remembers my answer. Then it proves the fix in a fresh container, with no model calls allowed. Only a clean pass counts.

**Beat 3, 0:45 to 1:25, neatlogs.** On screen: span tree, the Incidents list, the incident and its investigation, commit 2de852f, the MkDocs replay, the numbers table.

> neatlogs traces every run. [architecture] Each step is a span: planner, executor, recovery, verifier. [implementation] Three lines of setup, and a guardrail span on every budget check. [runtime] Here is a live run. [reasoning] On Saturday neatlogs raised an incident on my own agent. It counted 25 failed executions, 52.8 times the baseline, across 10 traces. The investigation named the cause at 66% confidence: a step runs cd, then the file check looks in the old folder. Commit 2de852f fixed it. [result] MkDocs went from a false fail to verified. A second investigation fixed invented planner steps, and finished runs went from 2 to 3 of 4. Cost per run went from $0.0262 to $0.0200.

**Beat 4, 1:25 to 1:55, Entire.** On screen: a commit's checkpoint on entire.io, `entire why`, the graph.

> I built FirstRun with Claude Code, and Entire recorded every session. [architecture] Each commit carries a checkpoint with the prompt and reasoning behind it. [implementation] I turned it on before the first commit. [runtime] Here is the session behind the recovery logic. [reasoning] Point `entire why` at any line, and you get the prompt that wrote it. [result] `<count>` checkpoints, and every line of FirstRun traces back to a decision.

**Beat 5, 1:55 to 2:25, cfo.ai.** On screen: the cfo.ai model, the scenario chart, a number's lineage.

> Then I planned the business with cfo.ai. [architecture] The cost per run is not a guess. It comes straight from neatlogs. [implementation] I gave Ari the plans and the measured cost. [runtime] Watch: what if the Team plan costs less? [reasoning] Margin holds, because one run costs `<cost>`. [result] At `<customers>` customers, revenue covers costs in month `<month>`.

**Beat 6, 2:25 to 2:50, recovery and proof.** On screen: a failed step, the retry, the clean re-run passing.

> Here a step failed: `<the real error>`. FirstRun classified it as a docs bug, found the fix, and retried. Then it ran the whole quickstart again in a fresh container. Green. That is the pull request it drafted.

**Beat 7, 2:50 to 3:00, the close.** On screen: FirstRun running on its own README, passing, then the end card.

> The last thing I did: I pointed FirstRun at its own README. It passed. Repo and traces are below.

## Record Each Beat as Its Own Clip

1. **Screen:** OBS Studio at 1920×1080, 30 fps. One scene per beat.
2. **Terminal:** the settings in `10 Brand and Design.md`, font size 18.
3. **Speed:** record real runs at normal speed. The `video-edit` skill speeds up the slow parts afterward.
4. **Voice:** record after the clips, reading the script above, in a quiet room with your normal mic. Read each beat 2 times and keep the better take.
5. **Order:** record beat 6 first, because it depends on a run that can fail on the day. Record beat 1 last.

## The Edit Follows Four Rules

The `video-edit` skill cuts it from the clips and the voice.

1. Cut every pause longer than 0.4 seconds.
2. Burn in captions, white on a dark bar, because most people watch muted.
3. Put a small step label in the top left corner of every beat, such as "neatlogs: reasoning", so judges can tick the 15 points while they watch.
4. Use no music under the voice, or music at 10% volume at most.

## The Thumbnail Shows One Broken Step

- **Size:** 1280×720.
- **Left side:** a real terminal crop with `step 4/7 ✗` in red.
- **Right side:** "Docs that work (literally)" in Inter 800, two lines.
- **Corner:** the `FirstRun▌` wordmark.
- **Made with:** the `social-cards` skill from the real screenshot.

## Upload With These Details

- **YouTube title:** "FirstRun: an agent that runs your quickstart before your users do | #neatHack"
- **Description:** the one-sentence pitch, the repo link, the neatlogs trace links, the cfo.ai plan link, and chapters at each beat start: 0:00, 0:15, 0:45, 1:25, 1:55, 2:25, 2:50.
- **Visibility:** public. Check that it plays in a logged-out window.
- **X:** the submission post must carry the demo link. If the draft also accepts a video file, attach the video natively too, because native video plays inline in the feed. If it does not, post the native video as the first reply.
- **LinkedIn:** upload the video natively in post 7.

# FirstRun Demo Video Shot Sheet

**Hook:** The dbt DuckDB guide never worked in a clean container. FirstRun found the broken step, fixed it, and proved the fix.

This sheet plans a 1:55 hero cut from three sources: DJI Action 4 footage, screen captures and motion graphics. It plans the shots only. Nothing here renders a video.

Every shot has an ID and a flag. `H` is human footage, `S` is a screen capture, and `M` is a motion graphic.

- **Stable** means the shot survives app changes. Shoot it once.
- **Re-shoot** means the shot shows FirstRun's own UI or CLI output. Shoot it again if that UI changes.

Every number below comes from the README, `hackathon.md`, the landing page or the dbt replay payload in `docs/examples/dbt.txt`. Do not add a number that is not in those files.

## The Film Follows One Real Bug for 1:55

One story runs the whole film: the dbt guide step `jafgen --years 6`. It breaks, FirstRun fixes it, a clean container proves the fix, and a PR goes upstream. The sponsor tools appear as the reasons each step worked.

| Time | Beat | On screen | Optional voiceover |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:07 | B1 Cold open | Night desk. A terminal turns red at step 10. | None. Keyboard, then an error thud. |
| 0:07 to 0:15 | B2 The problem | Laptop lid closes. Kinetic text. | "Your quickstart is the only part of your product tested by people who leave instead of filing a bug." |
| 0:15 to 0:22 | B3 The answer | Wordmark. Enter key in slow motion. | "So I built FirstRun. Give it a docs URL." |
| 0:22 to 0:44 | B4 Break | /run stages Read, Plan, Run. Step 10 goes red. | "It plans one step per command. Every step runs in a clean container. Step 10 breaks." |
| 0:44 to 1:02 | B5 Fix and prove | The diff. Prove stage at 9/9. The reaction. | "FirstRun calls it a docs bug and patches the step. A second clean container passes 9 of 9." |
| 1:02 to 1:12 | B6 When it broke | Bisect timeline, 0.3.1 green, 0.4.6 red, then the bisect comment on PR #10149. | "jafgen 0.4.6 dropped the flag, 11 months before the guide shipped. The bisect table went on the PR." |
| 1:12 to 1:25 | B7 Pull requests | Four real PR pages. Phone in hand. | "Every verified fix becomes a pull request. FirstRun opened 4 upstream." |
| 1:25 to 1:45 | B8 Three tools | neatlogs incident and its investigation, commit 2de852f, Entire checkpoint, cfo.ai cash chart. | "neatlogs raised an incident on my own agent and named the cause. Entire's review caught a fix that never ran. cfo.ai set the agent's budget." |
| 1:45 to 1:55 | B9 Close | Share popover, landing page, end card. Morning light. | "Docs that work. Literally. Replay the run at firstrun.atharvashah.com." |

The voiceover runs about 110 words, so the music carries the rest. The film also works with no voice, because the on-screen text carries every fact.

## Swap a Beat When the App Changes

Each beat is one block of shots with its own timing, so a change to the app costs one beat and never the whole film.

1. Check the `Flag` column in the shot checklist below.
2. Re-shoot only the `Re-shoot` shots inside the changed beat.
3. Keep the beat's length. Trim the new take to fit the old slot.
4. Rebuild a motion graphic only when a number in it changes.

Two changes are likely before Monday. The /run page lives on branch `site/run-overhaul` in `D:\Atharva\firstrun-run` and may not be live yet. A PR may also move from Open to Merged. A merged PR is good news, so re-shoot that page and keep it.

## Thirteen Camera Shots Put a Human in the Loop

You shoot alone, so every shot below is self-operated. Use the DJI Mimo app on your phone as the remote and the monitor.

**Night shots (B1, B2)** sell the problem. Keep the room dark and let the monitor light your face.

| ID | Shot | Mount and angle | FOV | Rate | Light | Length | Beat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H01 | Wide of you at the desk, room dark, terminal glow | Desk clamp on a shelf, behind and to the right | Wide | 4K 50 | Monitor plus one warm lamp in the background | 3 s | B1 |
| H02 | Your face as you read the error, a slow frown | Mini tripod below the monitor edge, low angle | Narrowest | 4K 50 | Monitor as the key light | 2 s | B1 |
| H03 | Fingers typing, keys at eye level | Mini tripod on the desk, 15 cm from the keyboard | Narrowest | 4K 100 | Keyboard backlight plus monitor | 2 s | B1, B3 |
| H04 | Your hand closes the laptop lid, then the chair rolls back | Low angle, side of the desk | Wide | 4K 50 | Monitor only, so the lid kills the light | 2 s | B2 |
| H05 | Coffee mug steam on the desk at night | Timelapse mode, mini tripod, 2 s interval for 20 minutes | Wide | Timelapse | Warm lamp | 2 s | B2 |

**Run shots (B3 to B5)** match the screen captures. Film the real command so the keystrokes match the terminal.

| ID | Shot | Mount and angle | FOV | Rate | Light | Length | Beat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H06 | POV typing `firstrun https://docs.getdbt.com/guides/duckdb` | Chest strap, camera tilted down to the keyboard | Wide | 4K 50 | Soft key at 45 degrees | 3 s | B3 |
| H07 | The Enter key, extreme close, in slow motion | Mini tripod at key height, 10 cm away | Narrowest | 4K 100 | Window daylight if you can, else the key light | 1 s | B3 |
| H08 | Over the shoulder as the steps run | Desk clamp behind your right shoulder | Wide | 4K 50 | Soft key plus the monitor | 3 s | B4 |
| H09 | You lean in toward the screen at the red step | Front, 30 degrees off axis, monitor-top clamp | Narrowest | 4K 50 | Soft key | 2 s | B4 |
| H10 | The "it passed" reaction: lean back, small fist, grin | Same as H09 | Narrowest | 4K 100 | Soft key | 2 s | B5 |

**Proof and close shots (B7, B9)** move into daylight. The light change shows that the problem is solved.

| ID | Shot | Mount and angle | FOV | Rate | Light | Length | Beat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H11 | Phone in hand, GitHub mobile app opens PR #10149 | Overhead, clamp on a boom arm or shelf | Narrowest | 4K 50 | Window daylight | 3 s | B7 |
| H12 | Sunrise through the window, desk in the foreground | Timelapse mode, mini tripod, 5 s interval for 40 minutes | Wide | Timelapse | Natural | 3 s | B9 |
| H13 | Slow push toward the laptop with the landing page open | Handheld, RockSteady on, walk in from 1.5 m | Wide | 4K 50 | Daylight plus soft key | 3 s | B9 |

Two honesty rules apply to the human footage.

- Act the reactions, but keep the screen content real. H10 must react to the real 9/9 Prove stage.
- Film the real PR in H11. Do not stage a fake push notification. If a maintainer comments before the shoot, film that real notification instead.

## Screen Captures Come in Two Kinds, Live and Plate

A **live capture** is an OBS recording of a real click or a real terminal run. A **plate** is a 2x screenshot that HyperFrames animates later with push-ins and pans. Plates stay sharp at any crop, so prefer them for every shot where no interaction matters.

**Capture setup for every S shot:**

- Record OBS at 50 fps on a 1920x1080 canvas, to match the 50 fps timeline.
- Run Chrome full screen (F11) in a Guest profile, with browser zoom at 125%.
- Turn on Do Not Disturb. Hide the bookmarks bar, the extensions and the taskbar.
- Set the terminal to a light theme, Geist Mono at size 20, 100 columns wide.
- Take landscape plates at viewport 1920x1080 with device scale 2, which gives 3840x2160.
- Take vertical plates at viewport 432x768 with device scale 2.5, which gives exactly 1080x1920.

**Cursor rules for live captures:**

- Set the Windows pointer size to 3, so the cursor reads on a phone.
- Move in straight lines at half your normal speed.
- Rest the cursor for 0.5 s before each click.
- Park the cursor off the content when you are not clicking.

### FirstRun's Own Pages and CLI Need a Re-Shoot After Each UI Change

| ID | Source | Action and cursor | Zoom target | Kind | Beat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Terminal: `firstrun https://docs.getdbt.com/guides/duckdb --fresh` | Type it live, press Enter, record the whole run | The step counter and the red step 10 line | Live | B3, B4 |
| S02 | `https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/run.html#ex=dbt`, Read stage | Open the page. Hold 2 s. Press the right arrow key. | The quoted docs sentence | Live | B4 |
| S03 | Same page, Plan stage | Press the right arrow key once. Hold 2 s. | The step list | Live | B4 |
| S04 | Same page, Run stage | Let the steps play. Press `j` to walk to step 10. | Step 10 turning red, `No such option: --years` | Live | B4 |
| S05 | `https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/run.html?s=10#ex=dbt` | Open the deep link. No clicks. | Step 10: the failure, the fix and the clean rerun | Plate | B4, B5 |
| S06 | Fix stage | Press the right arrow key. Hold 3 s on the diff. | `jafgen --years 6` to `jafgen 6` | Plate | B5 |
| S07 | Prove stage | Press the right arrow key. Hold 3 s. | The 9/9 fresh container result | Live | B5 |
| S08 | Docs graph stage | Click the step 10 node. The side panel opens. | The panel with the quoted sentence and the fix | Live | B6 |
| S09 | When did it break? stage | Hold 3 s. | The release timeline, 0.3.1 green and 0.4.6 red | Plate | B6 |
| S10 | What the docs assume stage | Hold 2 s. | git and Python 3.12 or later | Plate | B6, spare |
| S11 | Pull request stage | Hold 2 s. Open the Download menu. | The four files: report.md, patch.diff, pr_body.md, run.json | Live | B7 |
| S12 | Share popover | Click Share. Click Copy. Click "Copy link to this stage". | The popover and the toast | Live | B9 |
| S13 | `https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/`, hero | Scroll slowly from the hero to the film. | The chips "step 3/6 failed" and "6/6 verified" | Plate | B3, B9 |
| S14 | Landing page, "The Business Plan Found a Bug in the Agent" | Scroll to the cash chart. | Month 14 and the $0.028 cap | Plate | B8 |
| S15 | Terminal: `firstrun bisect <run> --package jafgen` | Type it live. | The last good and first bad release lines | Live | B6, spare |

S01 needs `--fresh`, because a URL tested in the last 24 hours returns the cached result. The dbt run took 18 minutes on 2026-10-10, so record all of it and speed-ramp in the edit. A fresh run can plan differently, so the replay page stays the source of truth for the story.

### External Pages Stay Stable

| ID | Source | Action and cursor | Zoom target | Kind | Beat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S16 | `https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149` | Scroll to the bisect comment. | The title, the +2 and -2 diff, the comment | Plate | B7 |

| S20 | neatlogs incident "Fix Planner Directory Change and File Verification Path Contradiction" | Open Incidents, open the incident, then click Show full report under Investigation. | The 52.8x spike line, the 10 traces, the 66% confidence ring and the root cause | Live | B8 |
| S23 | `https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/2de852f` | Scroll to the file check change. | The commit title "check files from where the step started" | Plate | B8 |
| S21 | `https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299` | Scroll the session slowly. | Checkpoint `01M4JGJ6NTE7YNB9Z0YW5FYVHN` | Plate | B8 |
| S22 | `https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE` | Open the cash forecast. | Cash going negative in month 14 under the old cap | Plate | B8 |

S20 needs a login. Hide your email and every API key field before you record. If a capture fails, the site screenshots in `D:\Atharva\firstrun\docs\assets\t-*.webp` work as fallback plates. The S20 fallback is `t-neatlogs-investigate.webp`.

## Motion Graphics Reuse the Launch Film and Add Real Numbers

The 44-second launch film at `D:\Atharva\firstrun\docs\assets\firstrun-launch.mp4` already holds the title card, "Break. Fix. Prove." and the three tool cards. Cut those segments in rather than rebuilding them. Build the new elements with the `video-make` skill in HyperFrames.

| ID | Element | Content | Flag | Beat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M01 | Error type-on | "Step 10" then `No such option: --years`, in red | Stable | B1 |
| M02 | Kinetic quote | "tested by people who leave instead of filing a bug" | Stable | B2 |
| M03 | Wordmark | Launch film title card: FirstRun, "Docs that work (literally)." | Stable | B3 |
| M04 | Stage rail | A pill in the top left: Read, Plan, Run, Fix, Prove | Re-shoot | B4, B5 |
| M05 | Error callout | A red underline on `--years`, label "removed in jafgen 0.4.6" | Stable | B4 |
| M06 | Diff | Red line `jafgen --years 6` slides out, green line `jafgen 6` slides in | Stable | B5 |
| M07 | Number trio | "9/9 in a fresh container", "10m to first success", "$0.03 this run" | Stable | B5 |
| M08 | Bisect timeline | 0.2.1, 0.3.1 green, 0.4.6, 0.4.10, 0.4.14 red, then "11 months" | Stable | B6 |

The real numbers for M10, one per tool:

- **neatlogs:** an incident counted 25 "Execution Failed" detections, 52.8x the baseline, across 10 traces. The investigation named the cause at 66% confidence: a step runs `cd`, then the file check looks in the old folder. Commit 2de852f fixed it, and MkDocs went from a false fail to verified.

M07 uses the dbt run itself: `time_to_first_success_s` is 600.4 and `cost_usd` is 0.03. Verify ran 9 of 9 steps. Step 7, `dbt docs serve`, starts a server, so FirstRun skipped it on purpose.

Logos come only from `D:\Atharva\NOTES\META\Attachments\neathack\logos\`. Never redraw or recolor one. That folder holds neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai only, so M11 uses text labels until you fetch official logos for the other four.

## Sound and Color Match the Site's Light Look

**Color.** The motion graphics use the live site tokens, which replaced the older ones in `10 Brand and Design.md`.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Page | `#F4F5F9` | Every motion background |
| Ink | `#1D1D1F` | Headlines and captions |
| Muted | `#65656B` | Labels |
| Pass | `#1B8A3A` | Passed steps, 9/9 |
| Fail | `#C4281C` | Step 10, the removed flag |
| Accent | `#0A66D6` | Links, the cursor, the stage rail |

Type is Geist for headlines and Geist Mono for commands and numbers. Animate with the site's ease, `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`.

The human footage follows a color arc. B1 and B2 stay cool and dark, with white balance locked at 5600K so the monitor glows blue. From B3 on, grade bright and low in contrast, with lifted shadows and white balance at 5000K. That arc lets the light world arrive with FirstRun.

**Music.** Use one track at 100 to 110 BPM, minimal electronic with soft plucks and a sub pulse.

1. Play a low pad with no drums from 0:00 to 0:15.
2. Drop the beat on the wordmark at 0:15.
3. Cut all sound for 0.5 s before the step 10 error, then hit the error thud.
4. Lift the track on the 9/9 reveal near 0:58.
5. Resolve on the end card at 1:52.

Duck the music 12 dB under the voiceover. The `video-edit` render normalizes the mix to -14 LUFS.

**Sound effects.** Record the keyboard with the Action 4 mic during H03 and H06, because real keys beat a library clack. Add a soft thud for the red step, a short chime for 9/9, and one notification ping in B7. Keep whooshes off the cuts, because the Apple look cuts hard on the beat.

**Captions.** Burn them in, because most people watch muted. Use Geist 600 in ink on a white pill, 2 lines at most, in the lower third. For the vertical cut, raise them about 90 px, because the Shorts interface covers the bottom.

**Transitions.** Use match cuts. The H07 Enter press cuts to S01 on the same frame the command runs. The H09 lean-in cuts to the red step 10. The H13 push toward the laptop dissolves into the S13 landing page plate.

## The Action 4 Shoots Everything at 50 Frames per Second

India runs on 50 Hz power, so room LEDs flicker on camera at 30, 60 and 120 fps. Shoot at 50 and 100 fps with a 1/100 shutter, and the flicker disappears. Edit on a 50 fps timeline, so 100 fps footage plays at half speed.

| Setting | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Resolution | 4K 16:9 | A center crop of 1215x2160 covers the 1080x1920 vertical cut |
| Normal rate | 50 fps | Matches the timeline and the 50 Hz lights |
| Slow motion rate | 100 fps | 2x slow on a 50 fps timeline |
| Shutter | 1/100 in Pro mode | Removes LED flicker at both rates |
| ISO | Cap at 1600 | Keeps night shots clean |
| White balance | Locked, 5600K at night, 5000K by day | Stops the color from drifting between takes |
| Color profile | Normal | Needs no grading time. Use D-Log M only if you will grade it. |
| Stabilization | RockSteady for H13, off on the tripod | A fixed shot needs no crop |
| FOV | Wide or the narrowest the menu offers | Ultra Wide bends the desk edges |

Frame every shot with the action in the middle third. Then one take serves both the landscape and the vertical cut.

Keep 4K 100 takes under 3 minutes. Long high-rate takes heat the camera indoors.

# neatlogs Evidence

Every FirstRun run is one `firstrun.run` WORKFLOW trace in neatlogs. Its spans are `read_docs` and `step.<id>` (TOOL), `planner` and `recover.<id>` (AGENT), `classify_failure` (TOOL), and `budget` and `verify` (GUARDRAIL). Bisect adds `firstrun.bisect` with a `probe.<version>` span per release. Prerequisite Proof adds a `prereqs.prove` GUARDRAIL.

## Before and After Traces Measure the Fix From Neatlogs

| Target | v1 trace | v2 trace |
|---|---|---|
| neatlogs Python SDK | `fccdbad9a9c6177b90112911fe485bd6` | `495d510fd6da5546dbc6ab6e52bcee68` |
| Entire install | `10c44df9626c19f5ac801f1c6d84610e` | `5520c5cff5e0ea61f130eced082b20c4` |
| Chroma getting started | `66ec093b00333fa221fade5d2fc5f55f` | `f63d2b842c2257ae8c340f6ce44e3848` |
| OpenAI v0 README (fixture) | `b98b419e286acf436083febdb5217cf9` | `78e538e63a65c5d00d0281effa119567` |

Per-trace spans, tool calls, cost and duration are in [before_after_traces.json](before_after_traces.json). The tag summaries are in [neatlogs_runs.json](neatlogs_runs.json).

## One Failed-and-Recovered Trace, Exported

[trace-recovered-entire-v2.md](trace-recovered-entire-v2.md) is trace `5520c5cff5e0ea61f130eced082b20c4`. Step 1 failed with `curl: command not found`, recovery installed curl in the container, step 2 failed until `~/.local/bin` was on `PATH`, and a fresh container then ran all 4 steps with no model calls. The trace status reads ERROR because a failed step span rolls up to the trace, while the run itself ended `verified`.

## Two Detections, One Investigate, One Fix Over MCP

1. Detection "docs step broke": a regex on TOOL span output, `command not found|No module named|unrecognized arguments|No matching distribution`.
2. Detection "planner invented a step": a regex on the `planner` span output. It flagged the planner spans of the Chroma, Entire and OpenAI v1 runs.
3. Investigate (Deep, workflow `firstrun`) traced the invented steps to the planner prompt: [neatlogs-investigation.md](neatlogs-investigation.md).
4. A Claude Code session read the detection and its trend over the neatlogs MCP server and applied the fix in commit `3ca6f11`.

## Three Alerts and One AI Evaluator Watch Every Run

Created over the neatlogs CLI on 2026-10-10. Each alert passed a dry-run test with email as the channel.

| Rule | Fires when | ID |
|---|---|---|
| firstrun p95 run cost above Scale cap | p95 `cost` is above $0.035 over 1 day, the $0.028 Scale cap plus 25% | `56b3b8be` |
| firstrun docs breakage or failed verification spike | 25 or more "docs step broke" hits, or 2 or more "Verification Error Monitor" hits, in 60 minutes | `74e5d64c` |
| firstrun budget guardrail tripped | each "Budget Limit Exceeded Alert" hit | `acd01964` |

The AI evaluator "report names the real failed step" (`a6aa683e`) is an agent judge with neatlogs MCP access, a $0.10 budget and 12 tool calls. It checks that the reported failed step matches the first failed TOOL span, that the failure class fits the container output, and that every patch has a passing verify run. Ad-hoc runs return `NOT_FOUND_OR_OPERATION_DISABLED`, so it scores through a scheduled evaluation.

## Evaluations, Sessions and a Second Evaluator Cover Runs and Audits

Set up over the neatlogs CLI on 2026-10-10, after the hackathon lifted plan limits.

**Sessions.** Every trace about one docs site shares the session `docs:<site>` and names the site as its end user, with the command (run, bisect, prereqs, audit) in the end-user metadata. One session shows a site's runs, bisects and audits together, and an evaluation can filter by site.

**A second evaluator.** "audit cards are backed by evidence" (`d1f7c5bb`) is an agent judge with neatlogs MCP access, a $0.10 budget and 12 tool calls. It reads a `firstrun.audit` trace and checks that the root summary matches the span outputs, that each card cites a commit or PR, and that each stale page cites commits on its topic. The audit root span now carries its cards and stale pages in `output.value` for this judge.

**Four evaluations.**

| Evaluation | Traces | Schedule | ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| FirstRun run review: backlog | every `firstrun.run` from 2026-10-10 | one pass | `0363e302` |
| FirstRun run review: every 6 hours | new `firstrun.run` traces | batch every 6 h | `57b7ff3f` |
| FirstRun audit review: backlog | every `firstrun.audit` from 2026-10-10 | one pass | `e16dd7cd` |
| FirstRun audit review: daily | new `firstrun.audit` traces | daily batch | `3122a1d3` |

The Public API cannot assign an AI evaluator to a form question, so each form and its evaluator are set in the dashboard before launch.

**A radar batch for the evaluations to judge.** `scripts/radar.py` ranked 70 Exa results with Jev, and FirstRun ran the top 18 official quickstarts in 3 parallel lanes, tagged `radar`, under the Team cost cap. Two runs exposed a FirstRun bug: a dev server step (`flask --app hello run`, `litestar run`) never exits, so it timed out. The fix passes a server step once its output says it listens. The `radar-v2` rerun took Flask from 0 of 4 steps to verified 4 of 4.

## The Integration Check Passed the Organizer's Gates

The organizers' setup prompt ran against this repo. Gates 1, 2, 3 and 5 pass and gate 4 is partial: [docs/neatlogs-integration.md](../docs/neatlogs-integration.md).
# neatlogs Investigate Result: Planner Invents Steps

Source: neatlogs Investigate (Deep mode, workflow `firstrun`, last 14 days), run by Atharva on 2026-10-10 after the "planner invented a step" detection flagged the planner spans of the Chroma, Entire and OpenAI v1 runs.

Question asked:

> Why does the planner agent add steps that are not in the docs, such as `true`, `command -v entire`, `test -f first_trace.py` and `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'`? It also skips the steps that need an API key, and the same neatlogs page produced 4 steps in one run and 3 in another.

Proposed fix, as neatlogs returned it: rewrite the system prompt of the `claude_agent.query` call in `planner.py`.

```text
You are an expert systems engineer and runbook generator. Your task is to extract installation and setup steps from the provided documentation Markdown and format them into a structured JSON runbook.

You must follow these strict rules to ensure reliability, safety, and determinism:

1. STRICT EXTRACTION ONLY (No Hallucinations):
   - You must ONLY extract commands that are explicitly written inside shell code blocks (e.g., ```bash, ```sh, ```shell) in the provided Markdown.
   - NEVER invent verification steps (such as `command -v <cmd>`, `test -f <file>`, `which <cmd>`) unless they are literally written as code blocks in the documentation.
   - If the documentation page is processed multiple times, it must produce the exact same steps every time.

2. PYTHON CODE & FILE EXECUTION (No `true` placeholding):
   - If the documentation contains a Python code block demonstrating how to run an example:
     a) Write the Python code to the specified file path (e.g., `quickstart.py`) using the `Files` schema field.
     b) Set the `Command` field of that step to execute the file: `python <filename>` (e.g., `python quickstart.py`).
     c) NEVER use `true` or other no-op shell placeholders as a command.

3. SAFE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES & SECRETS:
   - NEVER hardcode fake API keys, fake tokens, or mock secrets (e.g., NEVER output `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'` or `export MY_SECRET='abc'`).
   - If the documentation instructs setting an environment variable, use the variable itself as a safe placeholder: `export OPENAI_API_KEY="${OPENAI_API_KEY}"` or simply omit the export step if the runner environment is expected to already have it configured.
   - NEVER skip subsequent execution steps just because they require an API key or environment variable. Include them fully so they can run when a real key is provided.

4. STEP SCHEMA ALIGNMENT:
   Each step in your output must follow this structure:
   - Id: Sequential integer starting at 1.
   - Intent: A short description of what the step does.
   - Command: The exact shell command to execute (no dummy `true` commands).
   - Files (Optional): List of files to create before running the command.
   - Expected: Exit Code and expected output criteria.
```
# Entire Evidence

Entire recorded the agent session behind every commit, reviewed every layer on a Trail, mapped the repo for the build agents, and kept the decisions in Brain. Numbers below were read on 2026-10-10 at about 18:45 IST.

## Every Commit Carries the Session That Wrote It

- 49 checkpoint refs are on GitHub under `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`. Check with `git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*'`.
- Every normal commit carries an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer. Merge commits carry none, because Entire's hook skips merges.
- The neatlogs fix commit shows its whole session, from the MCP calls to the green tests: [checkpoint 01M4JGJ6NTE7YNB9Z0YW5FYVHN](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299).
- One checkpoint was lost: Git 2.33 hung the post-commit hook for 206 s on the scaffold commit. Git 2.55 fixed it, and no checkpoint was lost after that.

## Trails Reviewed Every Layer, and the Runners Found 3 Real Bugs

| Trail | Covers | Runner findings |
|---|---|---|
| [3](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/trails/3) | Layer 1, every commit from the scaffold to the wiring | 1 high, 1 medium, both fixed in e2aacb7 |
| [4](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/trails/4) | Layer 2: recovery, edge cases, the neatlogs fix | none blocking |

| [8](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/trails/8) to [12](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/trails/12) | Bisect, Prerequisite Proof, website, build log, README self-test | merged |

The 3 bugs the runners found:

1. **High:** a `needs_secret` step with its key already in the container retried the same command until the budget ran out.
2. **Medium:** the Docker command defaulted to the author's WSL setup, so FirstRun could not start containers on Linux or macOS.
3. **High:** the `cd` guard from d22eb69 was written and unit-tested but never called by `Container.exec`.

Each finding was resolved with `entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "fixed in <sha>"`.

## The Build Agents Searched the Repo Through the Graph

- `entire graph stats --repo .`: 10 graph calls, about 56,254 tokens saved, graph-first in 1 of 4 sessions. The first session started with grep, and the session noted it and switched.
- The full graph is in [graph.ndjson](graph.ndjson): 96 files and 1,526 symbols at the last Brain refresh.

## Brain Answers Why a Decision Was Made

`entire brain recall "why does recovery stop at 3 attempts"` returns the decision fact recorded during the build: a looping agent is the most common failure the neatlogs judges look for, so recovery stops at 3 attempts, 25 tool calls and $0.50 per run. Brain holds 7 such facts, from the Git version constraint to the one-trace-per-run rule.

## The Jury Self-Test Ranked the Repo With No Excluded Work

The Entire judge plugin, run on a fresh clone with the real start time, scored 3.93 of 5: authenticity 4.5, integrity 5.0, prompting 4.0, CLI awareness 4.5. The full report is [jury-selftest.txt](jury-selftest.txt). The test also found that `entire judge add` fetches only `refs/heads/entire/*`, while the default backend writes `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`. Brain's refresh fetched the refs on its own, so the repo was not dropped.

# FirstRun ### Docs that work. Literally. FirstRun runs your quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, and proves the fix with a second clean run. [![Live site](https://img.shields.io/badge/site-firstrun.atharvashah.com-0A66D6?style=for-the-badge)](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/) [![neatHack 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20for-%23neatHack%202026-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-246%20offline-1B8A3A?style=for-the-badge)](.github) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-3776AB?style=for-the-badge&logo=python&logoColor=white)](pyproject.toml) [**Try it in the browser**](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/) · [**Watch a real run**](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/run.html) · [**See the 4 upstream PRs**](#firstrun-found-4-real-docs-bugs-and-opened-4-upstream-prs) · [**Follow the build on X**](https://x.com/cultist_dev)
The 44-second launch film. The video does not play for you? [Open it on the site](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/) or [download the MP4](docs/assets/firstrun-launch.mp4).

```bash pip install git+https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun firstrun https://docs.example.com/quickstart ``` ## Break, Fix, Prove Takes 195 Seconds

1. Read
FirstRun reads the page and plans one step per command.
2. Run
Every step runs in a clean container, like a new developer. The first failure stops the run.
3. Prove
A fix is done only when a second clean container passes the whole quickstart.
The input below is a known-broken test fixture (`tests/fixtures/docs/broken_quickstart_FIXTURE.md`), not a real project's docs. Step 3 pins an old chromadb that cannot install on Python 3.11. ```text Step 3 of 4: pip install chromadb==0.3 ERROR: No matching distribution found for numpy~=1.21.6 Cause: docs_bug (source: jev) Patch: step 3 -> pip install chromadb Verified: 4/4 steps passed in a fresh container Time to first success: 195 s ``` FirstRun writes `report.md`, `patch.diff` and `pr_body.md` into the run folder. The patch is one line. ## Seven Teams Get a Different Job Out of the Same Engine | # | You are | The problem | Run this | You get | |---|---|---|---|---| | **1** | A DevRel or docs lead | Nobody tests the quickstart after launch day | `firstrun ` | A pass or a verified fix, with a PR draft | | **2** | A release manager | A new release of your package broke the docs and you do not know which one | `firstrun bisect --package ` | The last good and first bad release | | **3** | A technical writer | The docs assume tools the reader does not have | `firstrun prereqs ` | A Prerequisites block, proven in a clean container | | **4** | An open-source contributor | You want a first PR that a maintainer merges | `firstrun pr ` | The `gh` commands for the docs PR, source check included | | **5** | An engineer picking a tool | You want to know if the vendor's quickstart works before you commit | `firstrun ` | A time to first success and the first step that breaks | | **6** | A coding agent | You need a loop that checks its own docs work | `firstrun run --resume ` | State after every step and a model-free verify | | **7** | A head of docs | Hundreds of pages, and the code moved under some of them | `firstrun audit owner/repo` | Stale pages with the commits behind them, features with no docs, proposal cards and drafted release notes |
7. Which docs did the product outgrow? Audit the whole docs set from the git history. ```bash firstrun audit fastapi/typer ``` ```bash firstrun audit dbt-labs/dbt-core --docs-repo dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com ``` One blobless clone gives the whole history. The audit then works offline and costs $0 in model calls. Jev sorts commits with no conventional prefix when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set, and every audit is one neatlogs trace. - **Oldest first.** Every page, ranked by the date of its last edit. - **Stale or quiet.** A page is stale when product commits on its topic landed after its last edit, and the report names those commits. An old page that nothing changed under is quiet, so the team can leave it alone. - **Features with no docs.** Each user-facing commit in 120 days is checked against the docs text. A flag or name that no page mentions becomes a "Document this" card. - **Proposal cards.** Document this, refresh this page, feature this, create content around a feature with 3 or more commits, and automate the release notes. - **Drafts.** Release notes for the newest stable tag and up to 3 product highlights, written from commit subjects and pull request numbers. `firstrun audit-issue` turns the newest audit into `issue.md`, one checkbox per card, and prints the `gh issue create` command. It opens nothing on its own. To audit every week, copy [`examples/github-action/firstrun-audit.yml`](examples/github-action/firstrun-audit.yml) into `.github/workflows/`. Each Monday it audits the repo and updates one issue labeled `firstrun-audit`, so the docs team gets a fresh work list without anyone running a command. `--docs-repo` reads the docs from a second repo when the docs site lives apart from the code. Inside this repo, each audit is published to `docs/audits/` and opens at [audit.html](https://1run.netlify.app/audit.html).
1. Does my quickstart work today? Run it every night.
A DevRel team ships a quickstart once and a dependency moves the week after. The first person to find the break is a new user, and most new users leave instead of filing a bug. ```bash firstrun https://docs.example.com/quickstart ``` A clean pass ends as `passed`. A break ends as `verified` once a second container proves the fix. The nightly check costs $0.0167 per run on average over 64 runs, measured by neatlogs at list price.
2. Which release broke it, and when? Docs Bisect names the package version.
```bash firstrun bisect --package jafgen ``` FirstRun binary-searches the package's releases, one fresh container per probe, with the version pinned through `PIP_CONSTRAINT`. It replays stored commands, so a bisect makes no model calls. **Real result:** the dbt DuckDB guide never worked in a clean environment. Its step `jafgen --years 6` passes on jafgen 0.3.1 (2023-01-17) and fails on 0.4.6 (2024-04-07). PyPI has no release between them. The guide merged on 2025-03-14, 11 months after `--years` was gone. 5 probes found it.
3. What does it silently assume? Prerequisite Proof writes the missing block.
```bash firstrun prereqs ``` FirstRun turns the container fixes of a run into a Prerequisites block. Then it proves the block. A fresh container with only those items runs the docs as written. | Quickstart | The docs assume | Proof in a clean `python:3.11-slim` | |---|---|---| | AccuKnox knoxctl | curl, ca-certificates, gnupg, sudo | proven, 5/5 steps | | MkDocs | curl | proven, 9/9 steps | | Entire install | curl, git, `~/.local/bin` on `PATH` | proven, 4/4 steps, git found in round 2 | | dbt + DuckDB | Python 3.12 or later, git | steps 1 to 9 pass on `python:3.12-slim`, step 10 is the jafgen docs bug |
4. Open the docs PR. A verified fix becomes an upstream pull request.
```bash firstrun pr ``` FirstRun prints the `gh` commands and a PR body. Every draft gets a source check first, because a docs note can look like a docs bug. FirstRun opened 4 real PRs this way. They are listed [below](#firstrun-found-4-real-docs-bugs-and-opened-4-upstream-prs).
5. Test a vendor before you adopt it. Time to first success is the number.
Point FirstRun at any public quickstart. The report shows how long a new developer needs to reach a working result, and where they get stuck first.
6. Give your coding agent the loop. Plan, run, recover, verify, with a trace.
The site hands you a prompt for Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. The agent installs FirstRun, checks Docker, runs your quickstart, proves the fix and opens the PR when you say yes. `state.json` is written after every step, so a run resumes with `firstrun run --resume RUN_ID`.
## Radar Picks the Quickstarts Worth a Run, and the Run Log Picks the Buyers FirstRun spends model money on every run, so it should only run where a break is likely and someone will read the fix. 1. **Find.** Exa search returns candidate quickstart pages at no cost. 2. **Rank.** `scripts/radar.py` asks Jev 4 typed questions per page in one call: can it run unattended in a container, is a step likely to break, how many developers read it, and is it the official docs. Code multiplies the answers into one priority. No model reads the pages one by one. 3. **Run.** `firstrun run --targets targets-radar.txt --tag radar --tier team` runs the top pages in 3 parallel lanes under the plan-set cost cap. Every run is logged on the [runs page](https://1run.netlify.app/runs/). 4. **Sell.** `scripts/buyers.py` maps each docs site FirstRun ran on or audited to its company, enriches it through treg at $0.0018 a lookup, and asks Jev whether the company fits the $49 to $299 plan. The result is [business/buyers.md](business/buyers.md): companies FirstRun already has proof for, each linked to its replay. It holds company data only, with no people and no emails. ```bash python scripts/radar.py --from-exa exa_results/*.txt --top 20 ``` ```bash python scripts/buyers.py ``` ## FirstRun Found 4 Real Docs Bugs and Opened 4 Upstream PRs FirstRun ran five open-source quickstarts whose docs live in public repos. Every finding came from a verified run, where a second clean container passed with the fix.

dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com#10149
Fix the jafgen command in the DuckDB quickstart.
dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com#10150
State the Python version the DuckDB quickstart needs.
entireio/cli#2724
Say where install.sh puts entire on Linux.
| Quickstart | Result | What FirstRun found | Upstream | |---|---|---|---| | [dbt Core with DuckDB](https://docs.getdbt.com/guides/duckdb) | verified 9/10 | `jafgen --years 6` fails because `years` is now positional | [dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com#10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149) | | same guide | verified | the cloned repo pins `networkx==3.7`, which needs Python 3.12, and the guide names no version | [dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com#10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150) | | [Entire CLI install](https://docs.entire.io/installation) | verified 4/4 | `install.sh` puts `entire` in `~/.local/bin`, which a clean shell lacks on `PATH` | [entireio/cli#2724](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2724) | | [AccuKnox knoxctl](https://help.accuknox.com/knoxctl/) | verified 5/5 | the page names 0.9.0 as latest while the installer fetches 0.9.58, and the APT steps need `curl`, `gnupg` and `sudo` | [accuknox/help#671](https://github.com/accuknox/help/pull/671) | | [MkDocs getting started](https://www.mkdocs.org/getting-started/) | verified 9/10 | the docs commands work, the container needed `curl` | none needed | | [Dagster quickstart](https://docs.dagster.io/getting-started/quickstart) | verified 10/10 | the docs already cover both gaps FirstRun hit: install `create-dagster` first, and pip 25.1 for `--group` | none needed | On #10149, a bisect comment shows jafgen 0.4.6 dropped `--years` 11 months before the guide shipped. Replay any run in the browser at [firstrun.atharvashah.com](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/run.html). ## Built for #neatHack With Three Required Tools
[![neatHack 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/%23neatHack-2026-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) **A huge thanks to the [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) team for #neatHack.** One weekend, one solo build, and three tools that each did one job. No FirstRun code existed before kickoff on 2026-10-10 at 12:30 PM IST.

neatlogs

Traces every run.
The planner, executor and verifier show up as spans, so a bad run has a cause you can read.

Entire
