cfo.ai

Turns cost into a plan.
The measured cost per run from neatlogs goes into the pricing model. ### neatlogs Shows What the Agent Did Each run is one `firstrun.run` trace. The span kinds are WORKFLOW, AGENT, TOOL and GUARDRAIL. Claude calls appear as typed LLM spans.

One trace per run. Reading, planning, every step and verification sit under one root span.
A custom detection. "Docs step broke" flags failed tool spans. 40 flagged.

Detection analysis. 132 traces, 154 errors. "Docs step broke" hit 35 times, 12.9%.
Investigate. A 52.8x spike in Execution Failed opened a root cause with a confidence score.

Recovery spans. Classify, search, patch and retry show as `recover.N` spans.
Analytics. 132 traces and $0.9071 total cost, in one view.
Two detections run on the traces: "docs step broke" and "planner invented a step". The second one flagged 3 planner spans in v1. Investigate traced them to the planner prompt and proposed a stricter one ([evidence/neatlogs-investigation.md](evidence/neatlogs-investigation.md)). A Claude Code session read the detection and its trend over the neatlogs MCP server and applied the fix in commit 3ca6f11. The fix adds code guards that drop invented, placeholder and fake-secret steps. The integration check read 3 real runs back from persisted traces. See [docs/neatlogs-integration.md](docs/neatlogs-integration.md). ### Entire Records How the Build Happened

Checkpoint on every commit. Any commit maps back to the session that wrote it.
A merge gate. The merge stays blocked while a high finding is open.
Inline review. The finding sits on the line in src/firstrun/recovery.py.
- **Checkpoints:** every commit carries an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer. The neatlogs fix commit shows the full agent session behind it: [checkpoint 01M4JGJ6NTE7YNB9Z0YW5FYVHN](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299). - **Trail reviews:** Entire runners reviewed every layer on Trails 3 to 7. They raised 2 real bugs on Layer 1, a secret retry loop and a Windows-only Docker default, both fixed in e2aacb7. - **Trails:** [Trail 1](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/trails/1) covers Layer 1. - **Graph:** the build agents searched the repo through the graph. 4 graph calls saved about 11,662 tokens. - **Brain:** it holds 7 durable facts, such as why recovery stops at 3 attempts. Its last refresh indexed 63 files and 1,056 symbols. ### cfo.ai Prices the Nightly Check

Ari, the cfo.ai agent, on day one.		 The business plan sets the agent's spending limit. `firstrun econ` reads 64 neatlogs traces and writes [business/drivers.csv](business/drivers.csv) for cfo.ai. The mean run costs $0.0167, and the p95 run costs $0.0508. A 70% margin floor turns those costs into a cap per tier, and `firstrun run --tier scale` stops any run that spends past the cap. | Tier | Price | Quickstarts | Cap per run | Runs over the cap | |---|---|---|---|---| | Free | $0 | 1, weekly | $0.0108 | 48.4% | | Team | $49 a month | 10, nightly | $0.0471 | 7.8% | | Scale | $299 a month | 100, nightly, with PRs, Bisect and Prerequisite Proof | $0.0280 | 25.0% | The old fixed cap of $0.50 let one bad month cost a Scale customer's fee five times over. The plan, the Scale fix and every assumption are in [business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md](business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md). The cfo.ai model is public at [https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE](https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE). Under the old cap, cash goes negative in month 14.
## The Build Happened in Public on X Every step is a post on [@cultist_dev](https://x.com/cultist_dev). The five below tell the story in order.
**kickoff**
> #neatHack kickoff, 12:30 IST. FirstRun code before kickoff: 0 lines. neatlogs doctor probe: 7/7 PASS. Solo build. Submission opens Monday, 7 PM IST. [Read on X](https://twitter.com/cultist_dev/status/2108815318541844954) 		**day one**
> #neatHack, day one. all three required tools are up. Entire: trail #1 created. neatlogs: first agent trace, 3 steps, 12s. cfo.ai: Ari read my public profile. [Read on X](https://twitter.com/cultist_dev/status/2108826005854937357)
**the pitch**
> your quickstart is the only part of your product tested by people who leave instead of filing a bug. so for #neatHack i'm building FirstRun. break. fix. prove. [Watch on X](https://twitter.com/cultist_dev/status/2108828983194206308) 		**the plan**
> a quickstart breaks the way an agent breaks. quietly. so the plan for this weekend: every FirstRun run becomes a trace in @neatlogs. [Read on X](https://twitter.com/cultist_dev/status/2108856505566921210)
**the first catch**
> my neatlogs hackathon project has already caught doc issues for a chroma (24K+ github stars). chromadb's deprecated-config error sends you to its own migration guide. that page returns 404. [Read on X](https://twitter.com/cultist_dev/status/2108788557670125946)
## Run Your First Check in 5 Minutes You need: - Python 3.11 or newer. - Git. `pip install git+https://...` clones the repo, so it fails without git. - Docker. On Windows, run Docker inside WSL with the `Ubuntu-22.04` distro. - A Claude subscription token in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Create one with `claude setup-token`. - Optional: `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` for traces. - Optional: `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for Jev. Without it, Claude classifies the failure. Install: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun ``` FirstRun reads keys from `.env` in the folder you run it from. To use another file, set `FIRSTRUN_ENV_FILE`: ```bash export FIRSTRUN_ENV_FILE=/path/to/your/.env ``` FirstRun uses `docker` from your `PATH`. On Windows without it, FirstRun calls Docker inside WSL with `wsl -d Ubuntu-22.04 docker`. Set `FIRSTRUN_DOCKER` to use another command. Run it on a quickstart URL: ```bash firstrun https://docs.example.com/quickstart ``` A URL tested in the last 24 hours returns the cached result. Add `--fresh` to run it again. Read the result in `runs//report.md`. Build the HTML report with: ```bash firstrun report --html ``` Run it inside a clone of this repo and every run is logged for the public site. FirstRun writes the replay to `docs/runs/` and adds a row to `docs/runs/index.json`. Commit those files and the run appears on the [runs page](https://1run.netlify.app/runs/). Rebuild the log from the `runs/` folder with: ```bash firstrun publish --all ``` The offline test suite needs no network, Docker or keys. The tests ship with the repo, not with the pip package, so clone it first: ```bash git clone https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun ``` ```bash cd firstrun && pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest -q ``` FirstRun ran this section on itself in a clean `python:3.11-slim` container. The install failed until git was present, which is why git is listed above. The run step then stopped with the missing-token message, because a clean container has no Claude token or Docker. ## One Trace Follows the Docs Page From Read to Verified Fix ```mermaid flowchart TD A[docs URL] --> B["read_docs
Firecrawl · TOOL"] B --> C["planner
Claude Sonnet 5.5 · AGENT"] C --> D[runbook.json] D --> E["step.N in a fresh container
TOOL"] E --> F{step failed?} F -- no, next step --> E F -- no, last step --> I F -- yes --> G["classify_failure
Jev, ask once below 0.7, precedents.json · TOOL"] G --> H["recover.N
search, patch, max 3 attempts · AGENT"] H --> E H -- gave up --> J[report.md, failed] I["verify
new container, no model calls · GUARDRAIL"] --> K["report.md
patch.diff
pr_body.md"] ``` A `budget` GUARDRAIL span runs before every recovery. The root span `firstrun.run` is a WORKFLOW span that holds the whole tree. [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) lists the states, the failure classes, the budgets and every span. ## Each of the 8 Focus Areas Has a Feature You Can Open | Focus area | Feature | Where you see it | |---|---|---| | Planning | The planner turns the docs page into a runbook | `runbook.json`, the `planner` span | | Tool use | Firecrawl reads, Docker runs, Jev classifies | One TOOL span per call | | State | `state.json` is written after every step | `firstrun run --resume RUN_ID` | | Context | The planner reads only the quickstart page | `read_docs` span input | | Execution | One fresh container per run | `step.N` spans with exit codes | | Recovery | Classify, search, patch, retry up to 3 times | `recover.N` span | | Verification | A model-free re-run in a new container | `verify` span, status `verified` | | Iteration | v1 traces, detections, a fix, v2 traces | The results table below | ## Version 2 Finishes 3 of 4 Quickstarts and Recovers 3 Failed Steps v1 ran with recovery off. v2 ran after the neatlogs planner fix (3ca6f11), with recovery and verification on. The same four targets ran both times. Cost and duration come from the neatlogs traces in [evidence/before_after_traces.json](evidence/before_after_traces.json). # neatHack Build Log: FirstRun

## Project

- **Name:** FirstRun
- **Purpose:** FirstRun runs your quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, and proves the fix with a second clean run.
- **Problem:** Quickstarts break when a package is renamed, a flag is removed or a version moves. Nobody on the team gets an alert. The first person who finds the break is a new user, and most new users leave.

## Team

- Atharva Shah ([@HighnessAtharva](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva)), solo.

## Stack

| Part | Tool |
|---|---|
| Language | Python 3.11 |
| Agent | Claude Agent SDK, model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at medium effort, auth through `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` |
| Tracing | neatlogs Python SDK 1.4.26, neatlogs CLI 0.2.0 |
| Sandbox | Docker Engine 29.8.2 in WSL Ubuntu 22.04, one fresh container per run |
| Docs reader | Firecrawl CLI 1.25.3 |
| Failure classifier | Jev (TypeSafe System One) |
| Session capture | Entire CLI 0.11.4: Checkpoints, Graph, Brain, Trails |
| Business plan | cfo.ai |

## Planning Happened Before the Event

Planning and tool tests happened before the event in a private repo. No FirstRun code was written before kickoff (Sat 2026-10-10, 12:30 PM IST).

## Build Log

### 2026-10-10 (Saturday)

- **12:30 to 13:10 IST.** Created the public repo, ran `entire enable --agent claude-code --search-skill --agent-help-skill` before commit 1, and pushed the Entire config, 6 Trail runners, and the Graph and Brain agent instructions.
- **13:20 IST.** Preflight passed: 4 keys present (lengths only checked), Docker 29.8.2 in WSL, `gh`, Firecrawl 1.25.3, Entire 0.11.4, the venv on Python 3.11. `entire doctor` reports no problems.
- **13:30 IST.** Scaffold: `pyproject.toml`, `src/firstrun/config.py` (the only file that names a model), `src/firstrun/tracing.py`.
  - `python -m neatlogs doctor --probe` passed 8 of 8 checks, including `TRACE_VISIBLE` and `TRACE_FINALIZED`.
  - The first FirstRun trace, `firstrun.hello`, is trace `fdcab847f3129a251c6ae45f00c76a1c`. It is finalized with 2 spans and tag `hello`, and the neatlogs CLI read it back.

Entire state at the scaffold commit, run by the build agent:

```text
$ entire status
● Enabled · branch main
  Agents · Claude Code
  Checkpoints sync to: origin
1 session

$ entire checkpoint list
  branch       main
  checkpoints  0
No checkpoints found on this branch.
```

The checkpoint count is 0 because the scaffold commit is the first commit made inside an agent session. Later entries record the count after it.

- **12:55 IST. Entire checkpoints hung on Git 2.33.** The post-commit hook waited 206 s on `git update-ref --stdin` and the checkpoint for the scaffold commit was never written. Upgrading Git for Windows to 2.55.0 fixed it: the next hook took 3 s and the checkpoint landed.
- **13:00 to 13:35 IST. Six worker agents built FirstRun in parallel** on main, one track each: fixtures, planner, executor, recovery, verify and output, report page. Each track is one commit with its own checkpoint.
- **13:35 IST. Layer 1 done.** `firstrun run https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python` passed 4 of 4 steps in 70 s and wrote `report.md`. The first live run showed one run split into 3 neatlogs traces, so the CLI now opens one `firstrun.run` trace around reading, planning, every step and verification.

### v1 Runs, Layer 1 Only (Recovery Off), Tag `v1`

| Target | Result | Time | Cost (list price, not billed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs Python SDK | passed 3/3 | 84 s | $0.036 |
| Entire CLI install | failed at step 1: `curl: command not found` on python:3.11-slim | n/a | $0.023 |
| Chroma getting started | passed 3/3 | 250 s | $0.029 |
| OpenAI v0 README (FIXTURE, Wayback 2023-08-02) | failed at step 6: `openai: command not found`, the documented CLI is gone from today's SDK | n/a | $0.031 |

neatlogs v1 traces, one `firstrun.run` trace per run, cost as neatlogs measured it:

| Target | Trace ID | Spans | Tool spans | LLM calls | neatlogs cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | `fccdbad9a9c6177b90112911fe485bd6` | 9 | 4 | 1 | $0.0397 |
| Entire | `10c44df9626c19f5ac801f1c6d84610e` | 7 | 2 | 1 | $0.0170 |
| Chroma | `66ec093b00333fa221fade5d2fc5f55f` | 9 | 4 | 1 | $0.0217 |
| OpenAI v0 FIXTURE | `b98b419e286acf436083febdb5217cf9` | 12 | 7 | 1 | $0.0266 |

Six mistakes the agent itself made in v1. These are the "before" story:

1. **The plan changes between runs.** The same neatlogs page gave 4 steps at 13:35 and 3 steps at 13:40.
2. **The planner invents steps.** It added `command -v entire`, `command -v git-remote-entire` and `test -f first_trace.py`, which are not in the docs.
3. **The planner writes placeholder steps.** Chroma step 2 is `true`, a no-op standing in for "create the file".
4. **A fake secret passes as a step.** The OpenAI step `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'` exits 0, so it counts as a pass while proving nothing.
5. **The planner skips the step that matters.** It dropped the OpenAI `openai.ChatCompletion.create` example and the neatlogs "run your app" step because they need a key. Those are the steps most likely to break.
6. **Most expected results check only the exit code.** 9 of 16 steps have no output check, so a command that prints an error and exits 0 would pass.

### Saturday Afternoon: neatlogs Found the Agent's Own Bug, and v2 Fixed It

- **14:10 IST.** Atharva created two neatlogs detections: "docs step broke" (TOOL spans) and "planner invented a step" (the planner span). The second flagged the planner spans of 3 v1 runs.
- **14:40 IST.** neatlogs Investigate (Deep, workflow `firstrun`) traced the invented steps to the planner prompt and proposed a stricter one ([evidence/neatlogs-investigation.md](evidence/neatlogs-investigation.md)).
- **14:45 IST.** A headless Claude Code session read the detection and its trend over the neatlogs MCP server and applied the fix with code guards and a plan cache: commit 3ca6f11, checkpoint `01M4JGJ6NTE7YNB9Z0YW5FYVHN`, [Entire commit view](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299).
- **15:15 IST. v2 versus v1** on the same 4 targets: quickstarts finished 2 to 3 of 4, failed steps recovered 0 to 3, cost per run $0.0262 to $0.0200 (neatlogs). The v2 and real-world runs exposed 5 agent bugs, all fixed: a pipe that hid a missing `curl`, a multi-line step that hid a failing `pip`, pip noise that hid the real error, container fixes counted as docs bugs, and a file check after `cd`.

### Saturday Evening: Real Docs, Upstream PRs, and Entire Reviewing Every Layer

- **Real quickstarts:** dbt + DuckDB, AccuKnox knoxctl, Dagster, MkDocs and the Entire install all reached `verified` in a fresh container.
- **Upstream PRs, each from a verified run and a duplicate search:** [dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com#10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149) (`jafgen --years` removed), [#10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150) (Python 3.12 floor), [entireio/cli#2724](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2724) (Linux PATH after `install.sh`), [accuknox/help#671](https://github.com/accuknox/help/pull/671) (knoxctl page named 0.9.0 while the installer fetched 0.9.58).
- **No PR where the docs were right:** Dagster's page already covers both gaps FirstRun hit, so FirstRun opened nothing there. MkDocs needed only `curl` in the container.
- **Trails:** branch-backed Trails 3 to 8 cover every commit since kickoff. Entire runners raised 3 real bugs, all fixed and resolved with the commit SHA: a secret retry loop, a Windows-only Docker default, and a `cd` guard that was written but never called.
- **CI:** GitHub Actions runs the offline suite on every push. It caught 3 tests that passed only with a local Claude token.

### Saturday Night: Two New Answers From the Same Engine

- **Docs Bisect** (`firstrun bisect`): on the dbt guide, `jafgen --years 6` passes on jafgen 0.3.1 (2023-01-17) and fails on 0.4.6 (2024-04-07), and PyPI has no release between them. The guide merged on 2025-03-14, 11 months later. 5 probes, $0 in model calls. The evidence is a [comment on #10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149#issuecomment-6096827074).
- **Prerequisite Proof** (`firstrun prereqs`): proven blocks for AccuKnox (curl, ca-certificates, gnupg, sudo, 5/5 steps), MkDocs (curl, 9/9 steps) and Entire (curl, git, `~/.local/bin` on PATH, 4/4 steps).
- **Website:** [1run.netlify.app](https://1run.netlify.app) takes a docs URL and writes a prompt for the visitor's own coding agent. A tested URL shows its cached run first. Every run prints a share link that replays read, plan, run, fix, prove, plus the bisect timeline and the assumptions card.
- **Jury self-test:** the Entire judge plugin ranked the repo with no excluded work, 3.93 of 5 ([evidence/jury-selftest.txt](evidence/jury-selftest.txt)).

### 2026-10-10, 17:45 to 18:05 IST: The Business Plan Sets the Agent's Budget

- **Done: `firstrun econ`.** The command reads 64 `firstrun.run` traces from neatlogs and writes [business/drivers.csv](business/drivers.csv) and [business/unit_economics.json](business/unit_economics.json). Mean cost per run is $0.0167, p95 is $0.0508 and max is $0.1014. Each quantile row names its trace ID.
- **Finding:** the fixed $0.50 cap in `models.py` was 30 times the mean run. If every run hit it, Scale margin would be -403.6%. At a 70% margin floor, the Scale cap is $0.028, and 25.0% of measured runs cost more than that. [business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md](business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md) gives two fixes from the same formula: Scale at $529, or Scale at 1,500 runs.
- **Done: `firstrun run --tier NAME`.** The executor and the recovery agent check the tier's cap in the `budget` GUARDRAIL span.
- **Live runs on the typer quickstart, tag `tiercap`:**
  - `--tier scale` ($0.0280 cap): verified 7/7 steps in 127 s with 8 patches, at $0.0201 list price. neatlogs trace `9a29db323b3d054bb2c82e82e080340f`.
  - `--tier free` ($0.0108 cap): stopped at step 4 with `cost budget spent`, after 4 patches and $0.0114. neatlogs trace `06e7f3765141c2f417a862beef5f5134`.
- **Tests:** 255 passed and 2 skipped in the offline suite, including 8 new tests in `tests/test_econ.py`.
  - `--tier free` again, after the cap message moved to 4 decimals: stopped at step 4 with `cost budget spent: $0.0115 of $0.0108`. neatlogs trace `7060f5bd8dbb8cdc6c1dec3830ba7bab`.
- **Known gap: two cost counters.** On 43 runs matched by start time, FirstRun's own count totals $1.5253 and neatlogs totals $1.0989, so FirstRun counts 39% higher. The gap holds after the traces finalized, so ingestion lag does not explain it. The cap checks FirstRun's count, so it stops a run early and never late. Unifying the two counters is next.
- **Done later the same evening:** Ari built the cfo.ai model from `drivers.csv` over the `cfoai` MCP server, with 6 Scenarios. It is public at [cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE](https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE).

### 2026-10-10, 18:30 to 19:30 IST: The Docs Execution Graph

- **Done:** `run.html` draws a graph from the docs page, through every step, to the fresh-container proof. A failed step branches into its container output, its proposed fix, its rerun and its evidence. Clicking a node opens a side panel with the quoted docs sentence, the command, the output, the change, and every attempt before and after.
- **Honest labels:** nodes read Passed, Failed as written, Blocked, Not run, or Not run: out of scope. Red means the docs are wrong. Amber means the container lacked a prerequisite and the docs were fine.
- **Evidence path:** a toggle shows neatlogs trace, Entire checkpoint, Entire session, Trail and PRs in order. The checkpoint and session pages open without a login. The Trail and the neatlogs trace need one, and the page says so. Entire Graph is not used, because it maps code, not docs steps.
- **Example:** the dbt replay links step 3 to [#10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150) and step 10 to [#10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149) and its bisect comment.
- **Fixes found while building it:** the share tail kept pip download lines and dropped the real error, so stderr now goes last. `report.md` called the step that ended a run its "First Failed Step" even after recovery fixed an earlier failure. It now names both steps, and the root span carries `reported_failed_step` for the neatlogs eval.
- **Checked:** desktop at 1280 px and phone at 375 px with no sideways scroll, the dbt, Dagster and fixture codes, and no console errors. Offline suite: 260 passed, 2 skipped.

### 2026-10-10, 19:00 IST: neatlogs Alerts, an AI Evaluator, and Public Proof Upstream

- **Alerts, created over the neatlogs CLI with write scopes Atharva approved:** "firstrun p95 run cost above Scale cap" (p95 `cost` above $0.035 over 1 day, `56b3b8be`), "firstrun docs breakage or failed verification spike" (compound rule on 2 detections, `74e5d64c`) and "firstrun budget guardrail tripped" (each Budget Limit Exceeded hit, `acd01964`). All three send email. A dry-run test of each returned `simulated` for email.
- **AI evaluator:** "report names the real failed step", an agent judge with neatlogs MCP access, a $0.10 budget and 12 tool calls (`a6aa683e`). An ad-hoc run returned `NOT_FOUND_OR_OPERATION_DISABLED` with gate `tier-c-compute`, so scoring runs only through a scheduled evaluation.
- **cfo.ai:** Ari built the model over the `cfoai` MCP from `drivers.csv`. Under the old $0.50 Scale cap, cash goes negative in month 14. The figures are in [business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md](business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md).
- **Public proof on the 4 upstream PRs:** each got a comment linking the live replay, opened on the fixed step, and the public Entire session. The comments are on [dbt #10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149#issuecomment-6097945132), [dbt #10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150#issuecomment-6097945350), [Entire #2724](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2724#issuecomment-6097945657) and [AccuKnox #671](https://github.com/accuknox/help/pull/671#issuecomment-6097945911).

## Demo

"""neatlogs setup. Every FirstRun run is one trace."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

import neatlogs

from firstrun.config import load_env

_ready = False


def init_tracing(tags: list[str] | None = None, *, disable_export: bool | None = None) -> None:
    """Start neatlogs once per process. Tests set FIRSTRUN_NO_EXPORT=1 to keep spans local."""
    global _ready
    if _ready:
        return
    load_env()
    if disable_export is None:
        disable_export = os.environ.get("FIRSTRUN_NO_EXPORT") == "1" or not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY")
    if not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY") and os.environ.get("FIRSTRUN_NO_EXPORT") != "1":
        print("warning: NEATLOGS_API_KEY is missing. The run works, but no trace is exported.", file=sys.stderr)
    neatlogs.init(
        api_key=os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"),
        workflow_name="firstrun",
        tags=tags or [],
        debug=os.environ.get("FIRSTRUN_DEBUG") == "1",
        capture_logs=True,
        disable_export=disable_export,
    )
    _ready = True


def close_tracing() -> None:
    """Drain buffered spans. No shutdown here: it blocks on ingestion, and the SDK's atexit hook closes it."""
    try:
        neatlogs.flush()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        pass


def _json(value) -> str:
    import json

    try:
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return str(value)


def session_attrs(target: str, command: str, **meta) -> dict:
    """neatlogs session and end-user fields: every trace about one docs site lands in one session,
    and the docs site is the end user, so evals and alerts can filter by site."""
    return {"session_id": f"docs:{target}", "end_user_id": target,
            "end_user_metadata": {"command": command, **{k: v for k, v in meta.items() if v not in (None, "")}}}


def set_io(span, input=None, output=None) -> None:

        await p.wait_for_timeout(800)

    if full:
        h = await p.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollHeight")
        kw = {"full_page": True}
        # cap height
        if h > 7000:
            kw = {"clip": {"x":0,"y":0,"width":1920,"height":7000}, "full_page": True}

    await ctx.close()

        b = await pw.chromium.launch()

        async def guarded(j):

                try: await one(b, *j)
                except Exception as e: print("FAIL", j[0], e)
        await asyncio.gather(*[guarded(j) for j in JOBS])
        await b.close()
asyncio.run(main())

async def stages(b):

    p = await ctx.new_page()
    for n in NAMES:
        await p.goto(f"https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/doc-test/#ex=dbt&stage={n}", wait_until="load", timeout=90000)
        await p.wait_for_timeout(3500)

        await p.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        await p.screenshot(path=f"{OUT}\\st-{n}.png")
        print("ok", n, y)

async def site(b):

    p = await ctx.new_page()

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        b = await pw.chromium.launch()
        await asyncio.gather(stages(b), site(b))
        await b.close()
asyncio.run(main())

import json, subprocess, pathlib
d = json.load(open("script.json", encoding="utf-8"))
LEAD = 0.5
GAP = {"b1":1.0,"b2":0.9,"b3":0.8,"b4":1.1,"b5":1.1,"b6":1.1,"b7":1.0,"b8":0}
def dur(f): return float(subprocess.check_output(["ffprobe","-v","error","-show_entries","format=duration","-of","csv=p=0",f]).decode())
t = LEAD; out = {"beats": []}; parts = []
parts.append(("sil", LEAD))
for b in d["beats"]:
    a = json.load(open(f"{b['id']}.align.json"))
    al = a["alignment"]; text = a["text"]
    chars, st, en = al["characters"], al["character_start_times_seconds"], al["character_end_times_seconds"]
    assert "".join(chars) == text, b["id"]
    D = dur(f"{b['id']}.mp3")
    pos = 0; chunks = []
    for sp, disp in b["chunks"]:
        i0 = text.index(sp, pos); i1 = i0 + len(sp) - 1; pos = i1 + 1
        chunks.append({"text": disp, "s": round(t + st[i0], 3), "e": round(t + en[i1], 3)})
    # word times for cueing (spoken words)
    words = []; cur = ""; ws = None
    for c, s0, e0 in zip(chars, st, en):
        if c == " ":
            if cur: words.append({"w": cur, "s": round(t + ws, 3), "e": round(t + pe, 3)}); cur = ""
            continue
        if not cur: ws = s0
        cur += c; pe = e0
    if cur: words.append({"w": cur, "s": round(t + ws, 3), "e": round(t + pe, 3)})
    out["beats"].append({"id": b["id"], "name": b["name"], "start": round(t, 3), "end": round(t + D, 3), "chunks": chunks, "words": words})
    parts.append((f"{b['id']}.mp3", D))
    t += D
    if GAP[b["id"]]: parts.append(("sil", GAP[b["id"]])); t += GAP[b["id"]]
out["vo_end"] = round(t, 3)
json.dump(out, open("timing.json", "w"), indent=1)
# stitch
lst = []
for i, (f, D) in enumerate(parts):
    w = f"_p{i}.wav"
    if f == "sil":
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-y","-f","lavfi","-i","anullsrc=r=48000:cl=stereo","-t",str(D),w], check=True)
    else:
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-y","-i",f,"-ar","48000","-ac","2",w], check=True)
    lst.append(f"file '{w}'")
pathlib.Path("_list.txt").write_text("\n".join(lst))
subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-y","-f","concat","-safe","0","-i","_list.txt","-af","loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11","-ar","48000","vo_raw.wav"], check=True)
for p in pathlib.Path(".").glob("_p*.wav"): p.unlink()
print("vo_end", t)
for b in out["beats"]: print(b["id"], b["start"], b["end"])
EOF

cat > DESIGN.md <<'EOF'
# FirstRun demo video, design

## Style Prompt
Apple keynote style on a light canvas, matched to the live FirstRun site. One idea per scene. Real screen plates sit in white cards with soft shadows, and the camera pans and zooms inside them to the exact line the voice names. Motion graphics carry only real numbers. Green means a step passed, red means it broke, blue is the single accent.

## Colors (file 35, Sound and Color)
- Page `#F4F5F9`
- Card `#FFFFFF`
- Ink `#1D1D1F`
- Muted `#65656B`
- Pass `#1B8A3A`
- Fail `#C4281C`
- Accent `#0A66D6`

## Typography
- Geist for headlines, Geist Mono for commands, numbers and labels.
- Ease `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)` (site ease), GSAP `expo.out` as its stand-in.

## Layout
- Top-left label pill on every beat. Tool beats read `neatlogs · reasoning` and show 5 dots, one per rubric point.
- Plates live in y 120 to 880. Captions sit in a white pill in the lower third, y 900 to 1030, so they never cover a plate.

## What NOT to Do
- No dark canvas, no gradients on text, no neon.
- Never redraw or recolor the neatlogs, Entire or cfo.ai logos. Use the files in `assets/logos/`, copied from `NOTES/META/Attachments/neathack/logos/`.
- No number without a source file. VERIFY.md lists every number.
- No camera footage, no stock footage.
EOF
echo done

# YouTube Upload Details

Text only. Nothing here is uploaded or published.

## Title

FirstRun: an agent that runs your quickstart before your users do | #neatHack

## Description

FirstRun runs your quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, and proves the fix with a second clean run. Then it drafts the docs pull request.

On the real dbt DuckDB guide, step 10 (`jafgen --years 6`) fails. FirstRun patched it to `jafgen 6`, and a fresh container passed 9 of 9 run steps, with 1 server step skipped on purpose. Docs Bisect found the release that broke it: jafgen 0.4.6, 11 months before the guide shipped. FirstRun opened 4 upstream docs PRs.

Built solo for #neatHack 2026 with three tools, each with one job:
- neatlogs traces every run. It raised an incident on the agent itself (52.8x spike, 10 traces, cause named at 66% confidence), fixed in commit 2de852f.
- Entire records the Claude Code session behind every commit. Checkpoint 01M4JGJ6NTE7YNB9Z0YW5FYVHN holds the planner fix.
- cfo.ai turned 64 measured runs into the business plan. The old $0.50 cap ran out of cash in month 14, so the plan now sets the cap.

Try it: https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/
Repo: https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun
cfo.ai model: https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE
Replay of the dbt run: https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/run.html?s=10#ex=dbt
Entire checkpoint: https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299

The 4 upstream PRs:

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
